We have returned a mapped_rxn and template_id from first result. Need to ensure this corresponds to SN2 reaction? The description: SN2 substitution of halide by nucleophile forming C-N and breaking C-Cl. The template should involve halide broken and amine formed. The first result seems to involve a complex heterocycle, not simple SN2. Might not be correct. Need to find a template that matches SN2 on a halide to amine. The molecule: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. Contains a side chain with CN4CC(F)C4 (a tertiary amine with fluorine). There's a C-N bond maybe from a halide? Actually there is no halide in the molecule. The retrosynthetic step would break a C-N bond to form a halide? Wait SN2 forward: nucleophile (amine) attacks carbon bearing halide, displaces halide, forming C-N. In retrosynthesis, we break C-N bond to generate a halide precursor and amine nucleophile. So we need a template that breaks C-N (amine) and forms halide. Functional groups broken: halide (in forward) but in retrosynthesis we break C-N? The tool expects functional_groups_broken as those broken in forward reaction. So forward breaks halide (C-Cl) and forms amine. So we used broken halide, formed amine. That matches. The template found may be for amide? The first result's mapped_rxn shows product with OCH3 etc. Hard to parse. Might still be a SN2? The reaction seems to involve substitution of a halide on aromatic? Not sure.

We could verify if the template matches the molecule using check_smiles_reaction_template_matching. Use template_id 1014069.
